title: Power Query - Simply Explained
description:
If you clean the same spreadsheet by hand every month, Power Query can turn that ritual into a process that repeats itself. This beginner-friendly episode explains the four phases, applied steps, the M language, merge versus append and the habits that keep queries fast, for Excel and Power BI users who want to stop doing manual cleanup.
In this episode
00:00 – What Power Query actually is02:06 – Where you'll run into it03:06 – The problem it solves04:28 – The four phases and applied steps07:07 – The M language underneath the buttons08:18 – Merging, appending, data types and locale10:40 – Refresh11:43 – Where beginners go wrong and recap
Key takeaways
Power Query is the data transformation engine built into Excel, Power BI and other Microsoft tools, and every click becomes a recorded, replayable step.The workflow follows four phases—connect, transform, combine and load—and refresh reruns the saved steps without changing the source data.Setting data types (with locale) early, filtering at the top and understanding query folding keep queries correct and fast.
Worth quoting
“The real problem is that your clean up can't run itself again, so every new file drags you back to the same manual steps.” – Mirko Peters (03:44)
“The manual cleanup lives in your memory and disappears when you close the file, while the recorded one waits for you and runs again on demand.” – Mirko Peters (06:58)
